newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL rubber down on ringgit, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: KL rubber down on ringgit, trade quiet.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower on Monday after adjusting to the strengthening of the ringgit against the U.S. dollar, traders said.
There was no news of business, except for a consignment of SMR20 sold to Abu Dhabi on Friday, the traders said.
"The ringgit is the factor for the (price) adjustment," said a trader. "Otherwise, it's a quiet start to the week."
Government trade souces reported hearing a sale on Friday of 1,500 tonnes of August SMR20 to Abu Dhabi at 247.50 cents a kg.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the RSS1 for September buyer at 249.50 cents ($0.96) a kg, down one cent from Friday.
The SMR20 closed at 248.50, down 1.50 cents.
Dealers offered SMR CV at 293 cents, SMR L at 275, SMR 5 at 253, SMR 10 at 247 and SMR 20 at 245 and latex at 190.
The INRO's five-day average price was 192.75 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on August 1, compared to 192.06 on July 31. The daily indicator was 193.92 against 192.87.
